s1.syndrome_frame: pruritic skin lesions with systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory findings
salient_findings: pruritic lesions on arms and legs
right-sided headache, sinus pain, and congestion
key_facts: patient is a 75-year-old black woman
patient has insulin-dependent diabetes
patient has obesity
patient presented with a 10-day history of pruritic lesions
patient has a 2-3 month history of night sweats
patient has a 3-week history of right-sided headache, sinus pain, and congestion
skin lesions developed while patient was taking prednisone
patient has no associated fever, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, myalgia, or arthralgia
patient has dozens of 1-2 cm oedematous pink-red papules with a darker red-violet central zone
patient has about 20 red macules on the medial aspect of her feet and the tips of her fingers and toes
patient has one 2 mm erosion on the soft palate of her mouth
white blood cell count is 2.7 × 10⁹/L
haemoglobin is 100 g/L
platelet count is 129 × 10⁹/L
absolute neutrophil count is 1.4 × 10⁹/L
liver function tests are normal
urinalysis shows 2+ protein, no blood
PCR for herpes simplex virus, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody, and cryoglobulins is negative
antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody is negative
IgA levels are elevated at 8860 mg/L

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has pruritic skin lesions with vascular damage and extravasated erythrocytes, consistent with leukocytoclastic vasculitis.

shortlist.label: IgA vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has elevated IgA levels and skin lesions with vascular damage, consistent with IgA vasculitis.

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has target-like skin lesions, which are characteristic of erythema multiforme.

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has pruritic skin lesions and systemic symptoms such as night sweats and headache, consistent with Sweet syndrome.

shortlist.label: Cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has skin lesions with vascular damage and extravasated erythrocytes, consistent with cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis.

raw.rationale: The patient's elevated IgA levels and the presence of leukocytoclastic vasculitis on skin biopsy, along with the characteristic skin lesions, are consistent with IgA vasculitis.

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: While the patient has leukocytoclastic vasculitis on skin biopsy, the elevated IgA levels suggest a more specific diagnosis of IgA vasculitis.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: The patient's skin lesions do not have the typical targetoid appearance of erythema multiforme, and the presence of elevated IgA levels and leukocytoclastic vasculitis on biopsy are not characteristic of this condition.

rejected.label: Sweet syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's skin lesions and laboratory findings do not match the typical presentation of Sweet syndrome, which is characterized by fever, leukocytosis, and tender erythematous skin lesions.

rejected.label: Cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes IgA vasculitis, but the patient's specific findings and elevated IgA levels make IgA vasculitis a more specific and appropriate diagnosis.

gold: Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) with refractory anaemia with excess blasts-1 presenting with leukaemic vasculitis
